plan-goryokaku.hook: A perfect five-point star of snow, seen from 90 m above.
moments: Ride the fast lift up Goryokaku Tower to the deck at about 90 m.
Look straight down at the white star shape and the frozen moat around it.
Stand on the glass floor panel and look at the ground far below your feet.
Walk into the fort and see the Hakodate Magistrate's Office, a wooden building rebuilt in 2010.
Find the statue of Hijikata Toshizo, the Shinsengumi leader who died in this war in 1869.
plan-goryokaku.tip: Go up near sunset. In winter the 'Hoshi no Yume' lights outline the star after dark, so you see it by day and night.

plan-onuma.hook: Catch small fish through a hole in a frozen lake, then eat them fried.
moments: Walk onto the frozen lake with volcano Komagatake standing white behind the small islands.
Sit in a fishing tent over a hole in the ice and pull up tiny wakasagi smelt.
Eat your catch as hot, crispy tempura right after fishing.
Ride a snowmobile across the snowy lake if you want speed.
Buy a box of Onuma dango at Numanoya, made since 1905: soy and red bean, or soy and sesame.
plan-onuma.tip: The dango box is shaped like the two lakes, with the dango as the islands. Eat it the same day; it goes hard.

plan-niseko.hook: Deep, dry powder snow with Mt Yotei standing in front of every run.
moments: Take the first lift and ski fresh powder while the snow is still soft and untouched.
Stop on the slope and look across the valley at Mt Yotei, a perfect white cone.
Ski the Hanazono tree runs through birch forest (good skier) on the all-mountain pass.
Practice turns on the gentle slopes by the Ace Family lift in an English group lesson (beginner).
Ski under the lights at night, with snow falling through the lamp beams.
plan-niseko.tip: Powder is best in the first two hours. Eat dinner in Kutchan town; it costs much less than Hirafu village.

plan-otaru-canal.hook: Stone warehouses, gas lamps and snow: an old harbor town at dusk.
moments: Stand on Asakusa Bridge for the classic view down the canal with the warehouses on the left.
Walk the stone path by the water as the gas lamps turn on one by one.
Watch the snow on the warehouse roofs turn blue, then orange in the lamp light.
Warm up with a local beer inside Otaru Soko No.1, a brewery in an old canal warehouse.
plan-otaru-canal.tip: Arrive at about 16:00, before the lamps come on at about 16:30. You get the blue sky and the lights in one visit.

plan-sakaimachi.hook: A snowy street of glass lamps, music boxes and a whistling steam clock.
moments: Walk into Kitaichi Hall, a dark old warehouse lit only by 167 oil lamps.
Look through the Kitaichi Glass shops for hand-made glass cups and small lamps.
Eat LeTAO's Double Fromage cheesecake, soft and cold, at the main shop.
Stand at the steam clock outside the Music Box Museum and hear it whistle a tune every 15 minutes.
Listen inside the music box museum, where thousands of small boxes play at once.
plan-sakaimachi.tip: Be at the steam clock on the hour; it also lets out a big cloud of steam then. Walk slowly, the street is icy.

plan-otaru-sushi.hook: Winter fish from the port, cut in front of you at the counter.
moments: Walk up Sushi-ya Dori and choose from about 20 small sushi shops.
Sit at the counter and watch the chef slice fish from the Otaru port.
Eat a lunch set of nigiri with sea urchin, salmon roe and local white fish.
Finish with a hot bowl of miso soup while snow falls outside.
plan-otaru-sushi.tip: Go at lunch; the same sets cost much less than at dinner. Ask the chef for 'jizakana', the local fish of the day.

plan-ramen-mura.hook: Eight Asahikawa ramen shops in one building, hot bowls in deep cold.
moments: Walk the row of eight shops and pick the two that look best to you.
Order a mini bowl of shoyu ramen with pork and seafood soup.
See the thin layer of lard on top that keeps the soup hot to the last sip.
Taste the firm, wavy Asahikawa noodles, then walk to the next shop for bowl two.
plan-ramen-mura.tip: Order the mini size (ミニ) at each shop. Some shops close early now, so arrive before 19:00.

plan-asahiyama.hook: King penguins walk past you through the snow, close enough to touch.
moments: Stand in the front row by 10:40 and wait for the penguins to come out.
Watch the king penguins walk in a line through the snow, only one step from you.
Walk through the glass tunnel under the penguin pool and watch them fly through the water.
Put your head up into the small glass dome in the polar bear area and see a bear look at you.
Watch seals swim up and down the tall glass tube in the seal house.
plan-asahiyama.tip: Stand on the route by 10:40. The walk is at 11:00 and 14:30; it can stop if the weather is bad.

plan-blue-pond.hook: A frozen pond with dead trees, lit in changing colors at night.
moments: Walk about five minutes on packed snow from the car park, in the dark and quiet.
See the snow-covered pond and the tall dead larch trees standing in it.
Watch the lights change the trees and snow from blue to purple to green.
Feel the cold at about -15°C, and hear only the crunch of snow under your boots.
plan-blue-pond.tip: Wear boots with grip and your warmest layers. Stand at the end of the path for a clear view of the tree line.

plan-shirahige.hook: Water pours out of a cliff into a river that is bright blue.
moments: Walk onto Shirogane Bridge, called the Blue River Bridge, in Shirogane Onsen.
Look down at the 30 m falls pouring out of the rock face, not from a river above.
See the blue water between white snow and ice on the rocks.
Stay as the lights come on and the blue river glows at dusk.
plan-shirahige.tip: Come at dusk, before the Blue Pond. You see the blue color in the last daylight, then the night lights.

plan-beer-museum.hook: Drink a beer made to an 1877 recipe in a red-brick building from 1890.
moments: Walk up to the red-brick building with the red star on top, the old Kaitakushi symbol.
Follow the Premium Tour guide through the history of Japan's oldest beer brand.
Taste two beers in the Premium Lounge: Black Label and the reproduced 'Sapporo Seibakushu'.
Walk next door to the Beer Garden and grill all-you-can-eat Jingisukan lamb with beer.
plan-beer-museum.tip: Book the Premium Tour online. It is for people 20 and over only and takes about 70 minutes. Closed on Mondays.

plan-daruma.hook: Sapporo's lamb grill since 1954: smoke, fat and a tiny counter.
moments: Wait in the queue outside in the snow, then squeeze onto a stool at the counter.
Watch the staff put a piece of fat on top of the hot dome-shaped iron pan.
Grill lamb on the dome while onions and leeks cook in the juices at the edge.
Dip the lamb in the sweet soy sauce and eat it with rice and kimchi.
Ask for hot tea in your leftover sauce at the end and drink it like soup.
plan-daruma.tip: The queue is shorter after 22:00. Wear clothes you do not mind; they will smell of lamb smoke.

plan-nijo.hook: A seafood breakfast bowl heavy with crab, sea urchin and salmon roe.
moments: Walk the market street past boiled hairy crabs and king crab legs on ice.
Sit in a small shop and order a rice bowl with uni, crab and ikura.
Pop the orange salmon roe on your tongue and taste the sweet uni.
Try grilled scallops or crab from a stall on the street.
plan-nijo.tip: Go early, before 09:00. Shops are quieter and the seafood is fresh. Check the price of each bowl before you order.

plan-garaku.hook: Sapporo's own curry: a thin spicy soup full of big pieces of meat.
moments: Take a number from the machine at the door and walk around until your turn.
Choose your spice level and your soup, based on Japanese dashi stock.
Eat the soft chicken leg or the grilled pork kakuni with big grilled vegetables.
Dip spoonfuls of rice into the hot soup and feel the spice warm you up.
plan-garaku.tip: Start with a low spice level. The number system lets you shop nearby instead of standing in the cold.

plan-odori.hook: Watch giant snow sculptures being built for the Snow Festival.
moments: Go up Sapporo TV Tower to the deck at about 90 m, above the east end of Odori Park.
Look down along the long white park toward the mountains in the west.
Walk the park blocks and watch trucks, cranes and teams shape huge blocks of snow.
See wooden frames and scaffolding around sculptures the size of buildings.
plan-odori.tip: Go up the TV Tower first for the full view, then walk the park west. Do not enter the fenced work areas.

plan-moiwa.hook: All of Sapporo lit below you from a 531 m mountain top.
moments: Ride the ropeway up the snowy mountain, then the small cable car to the summit.
Watch the sunset at about 16:45 as the sky turns orange over the city.
Stay as the city lights come on and fill the whole plain below.
Ring the bell at the top of the deck, a favorite spot for couples.
Warm up with a drink in The Jewels restaurant, next to the big windows.
plan-moiwa.tip: Arrive by 16:15 to see sunset and the night view. Buy the priority ticket in the evening to skip the queue.
